Prevention: Burn the crop residue from the previous crop and then mix in soil
Rotate crop after one year or more (e.g. with sesame, rice or pulses)
Use furrow or drip irrigation; do not use overhead irrigation
Avoid splashing – use plastic sheet as mulch

Seed treatments with fungicides to prevent disease (see yellow direct control); Hot water treatment : soaking seeds in water at 45°C for ten minutes may help to reduce seed transmission but does not eliminate the pathogen; do not use hot water method if seeds are already treated with fungicides
Monitoring: Where to look for the problem:
Upper surface of young leaves (pale green to light yellow spots).
Look for rectangular or angular spots, especially on the lower leaves of the plant.
Spots tend to be on or close to the veins
If possible, confirm by microscopic examination.
Look for sporangiophores and sporangia in leaves
Plants are in a vegetative stage
When weather conditions favour the disease (high humidity and temperature of 20-22°C)
When to consider taking action: 10-25% infested leaves per acre [sample 20 plants from infected field]
Direct Control: Physical control: hand picking of infected leaves
Apply biopesticide, Trichoderma , harzianum available from the
T. harzianum , rice bran and water is kept overnight by covering with plastic sheet
Apply the mixture into the soil of the infested field
Restrictions: Maximum number of application times: 2-3 times.
